title: Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert
function: Thermal barrier piston core insert for disc caliper
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this brake caliper hardware application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by thermal barrier piston core insert for disc caliper and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for brake caliper hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g at 200W fiber laser
Go/No-Go ring gauging at 200W fiber laser
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for thermal barrier piston application
commonFailures: Thread galling Ti-on-Ti assembly - prevented by MoS2 anti-seize compound and -20% installation torque — critical for thermal barrier piston performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert suitable for Thermal barrier piston core insert for disc caliper?
faq.a: Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address brake caliper hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for thermal barrier piston requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. thermal barrier piston components require Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for thermal barrier piston application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Brake Caliper Piston Insert includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet thermal barrier piston specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
